value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Placement companies (P3MI) need a licence (SIP3MI) and a deposit and are liable for placement duties and sanctions; the 2017 Law does not make them jointly liable with the employer for wages abroad.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: Workers may not be charged placement costs in law (Art. 30), but BP2MI Regulation 9/2020 exempts only ten occupations (among them domestic workers, caregivers, farm workers, fishing crew and drivers); implementation was postponed in 2021 for lack of funding, and fees in other occupations follow destination cost structures.
source: Law 18/2017 Art. 30; BP2MI Reg. 9/2020; BP2MI Decision 214/2021

value_label: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
note: A placement agreement and an employment contract must be signed before departure; contracts are verified by the mission in the destination country.

value_label: Orientation on rights and complaint channels is compulsory and free of charge to the worker
note: Pre-departure orientation (OPP) is compulsory and run by the government; the 2017 Law lists it among costs the worker does not bear.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: Compulsory BPJS Ketenagakerjaan coverage for work accidents and death before, during and after placement, with benefits for repatriation and failed placement; missions provide legal assistance.

value_label: A statute requires labor or welfare officers in missions in the main destination countries
note: The 2017 Law requires the government to place labor attachés in missions in destination countries.

value_label: Complaints lead to administrative sanctions or refunds of fees, but compensation needs the ordinary courts
note: Disputes are settled by deliberation, then through the courts; KP2MI and the Ministry impose administrative sanctions on P3MI, and Law 21/2007 provides criminal remedies and restitution for trafficking.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions by destination or occupation, or minimum ages above 18, that are sex-neutral on their face
note: Minimum age 18. Since 2015 placement of workers with individual employers (domestic work) in 19 Middle Eastern countries has been halted, except through a pilot one-channel system; reports in 2023 that the halt was lifted are contradicted by later official statements, so its status is to be confirmed. The rule is sex-neutral on its face, although almost all domestic workers are women.
source: Manpower Decision 260/2015; Manpower Decision 291/2018; Antara and Bisnis.com, 2023–2025

value_label: A statute assigns a public body the duty to provide reintegration services (employment, financial, psychosocial) to returning workers
note: Central and district governments must provide social and economic empowerment for returning workers and their families; KP2MI runs reintegration programs.

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed, and the law makes the agency liable jointly with the foreign employer for the worker's claims
note: Licensing by the Department of Migrant Workers; agencies are jointly and solidarily liable with the foreign employer for claims arising from the contract, and corporate officers are personally liable.
source: RA 8042 sec. 10 as amended by RA 10022

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: The placement fee is capped at one month's salary; no fee may be charged to household service workers (since 2006), to seafarers, or where the destination prohibits charging workers.

value_label: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
note: Deployment requires a standard employment contract approved by the Department, verified by the Migrant Workers Office for direct and agency hires.

value_label: Orientation on rights and complaint channels is compulsory and free of charge to the worker
note: Pre-employment and pre-departure orientation seminars are compulsory; OWWA provides them free to most workers.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: OWWA membership covers death, disability and repatriation and funds legal and welfare assistance; agency-hired workers also have compulsory insurance paid by the agency.

value_label: A statute requires labor or welfare officers in missions in the main destination countries
note: Migrant Workers Offices with labor attachés and welfare officers are established by statute in destination countries.

value_label: A specialized body at home can award compensation to workers against recruiters (and employers abroad) for breaches during recruitment or employment
note: Labor arbiters of the National Labor Relations Commission hear money claims of overseas workers against the agency and the employer jointly; the Department adjudicates recruitment violations.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions by destination or occupation, or minimum ages above 18, that are sex-neutral on their face
note: Deployment is allowed only to countries certified as protecting migrant workers, and bans or suspensions for named destinations have been used (for example Kuwait in 2018 and 2023). Household service workers must meet a minimum age set by rules (reported as 23 or 25; to be checked), sex-neutral on its face.
source: RA 10022 sec. 3; DMW advisories; Governing Board Resolution (2006)

value_label: A statute assigns a public body the duty to provide reintegration services (employment, financial, psychosocial) to returning workers
note: The National Reintegration Center for OFWs, now within the Department of Migrant Workers, has a statutory mandate for reintegration services.

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Service enterprises need a licence, legal capital and a deposit; they answer for their own obligations and must settle the worker's rights if the employer defaults in some cases, but no general joint liability with the employer is written in the Law.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: Service fees are capped (in general one month's salary per 12 months, at most three months' salary) and must be agreed after the supply contract is signed; the 2020 Law removed the worker's duty to refund brokerage commissions; the fee cap is zero for Japan under the 2024 amendment.
source: Law 69/2020 Art. 23; Circular 21/2021 as amended by Circular 02/2024 and Circular 09/2026

value_label: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
note: A written contract with statutory minimum content is required, and the supply contract must be registered with or approved by the authority before workers are recruited.

value_label: Orientation is compulsory but may be charged to the worker, or compulsory only for some categories
note: Orientation education with a completion certificate is compulsory before departure; the cost may be collected from the worker.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: Workers and enterprises contribute to the Overseas Employment Support Fund, which supports workers who die, are injured or must return early and funds legal support; social insurance also applies.

value_label: A statute requires labor or welfare officers in missions in the main destination countries
note: The Law provides for labor management sections in missions in countries receiving Vietnamese workers.

value_label: Complaints lead to administrative sanctions or refunds of fees, but compensation needs the ordinary courts
note: Complaints go to the authority, which can sanction enterprises and order refunds; compensation claims go to the courts.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions by destination or occupation, or minimum ages above 18, that are sex-neutral on their face
note: Minimum age 18; the Law lists prohibited jobs and areas (for example some jobs in nightlife and in conflict zones), sex-neutral on their face.
source: Law 69/2020 Art. 7, Appendix (prohibited jobs and areas)

value_label: A statute assigns a public body the duty to provide reintegration services (employment, financial, psychosocial) to returning workers
note: The state supports returning workers with job counseling, referral and self-employment loans through employment service centers.

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Recruiting agencies need a licence and a deposit; they must compensate workers if the work or pay differs from the agreement, but the Act does not make them jointly liable with the employer as such.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: Service charges are capped; under the 2015 'free visa, free ticket' decision employers in Malaysia and six Gulf states pay visa and air ticket and agencies may charge at most NPR 10,000; zero cost under government schemes.

value_label: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
note: A labor approval requires an employment contract with stated minimum terms, attested where required.

value_label: Orientation is compulsory but may be charged to the worker, or compulsory only for some categories
note: Orientation training is compulsory before labor approval; workers pay a fee to approved training centers.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: Contributions to the Foreign Employment Welfare Fund and compulsory insurance are conditions of approval; the Fund pays for death, injury and repatriation and supports families.

value_label: A statute requires labor or welfare officers in missions in the main destination countries
note: The Act requires labor attachés in countries with large numbers of Nepali workers (more than 5,000).

value_label: A specialized body at home can award compensation to workers against recruiters (and employers abroad) for breaches during recruitment or employment
note: The Department can order compensation against agencies and the Foreign Employment Tribunal tries offenses under the Act and can order compensation.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions whose terms apply to women only (higher minimum ages, consent requirements, bans)
note: Rules on domestic work abroad have applied to women only: a minimum age of 30 (2012), then 24 (2015), and suspensions of domestic work in Gulf destinations since 2016, with conditions set in 2020. Current status is to be confirmed with the Department of Foreign Employment.
source: Guidelines for sending domestic workers 2074 (2017); Kathmandu Post 2015–2018; HRW 2021

value_label: Reintegration rests on policy or programs without a statutory duty
note: Reintegration services run through the Foreign Employment Board and local governments under policy and programs; no statutory duty was found in the Act.

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Recruiting agents need a licence and a security deposit and may be sanctioned; the Act and the 2019 Rules regulate sub-agents, but agents are not made jointly liable for the employer's obligations.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: The government sets a maximum migration cost for each destination (for example for Saudi Arabia and Malaysia); charging more is an offense.

value_label: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
note: Emigration clearance requires an employment contract with stated terms, attested by the mission where required.

value_label: Orientation is compulsory but may be charged to the worker, or compulsory only for some categories
note: Pre-departure briefing is required for clearance; longer training is required for women going into domestic work; whether all of it is free to the worker is not established.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: The Wage Earners' Welfare Fund, financed by compulsory contributions, pays death and disability benefits, repatriation of bodies and legal assistance.

value_label: A statute requires labor or welfare officers in missions in the main destination countries
note: The Act provides for labor welfare wings in missions in destination countries.

value_label: A specialized body at home can award compensation to workers against recruiters (and employers abroad) for breaches during recruitment or employment
note: A worker may complain to the government, which may settle the matter by arbitration and order compensation; offenses can also be prosecuted.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions whose terms apply to women only (higher minimum ages, consent requirements, bans)
note: Women going abroad for domestic work must be at least 25 (with an upper age limit in some recruitment rounds); the rule applies to women only. Current wording to be confirmed with BMET.
source: BMET guidelines; Daily Star and Financial Express reports

value_label: A statute assigns a public body the duty to provide reintegration services (employment, financial, psychosocial) to returning workers
note: The Wage Earners' Welfare Board has statutory functions on rehabilitation and reintegration; Probashi Kallyan Bank provides reintegration loans.
source: Wage Earners' Welfare Board Act 2018; OEMP 2016

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Recruiting agents must register and furnish a bank guarantee that can be forfeited; no joint liability with the employer.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: Service charges are capped by the Rules (at present ₹30,000 including tax); no cap applies to emigrants who do not need emigration clearance.

value_label: A contract is required, but only for some categories of workers, or without minimum terms or verification
note: Clearance requires a contract only for holders of ECR passports going to the 18 listed countries; other workers emigrate without state review of the contract.

value_label: No compulsory orientation
note: Pre-departure orientation (PDOT) is offered but is not a condition of emigration.

value_label: Coverage is limited to some categories of workers or to some of these risks
note: The Pravasi Bharatiya Bima Yojana is compulsory only for ECR workers (death and permanent disability up to ₹10 lakh, repatriation, legal expenses); the Indian Community Welfare Fund at missions rests on guidelines.

value_label: Officers are posted by administrative decision or policy, without a statutory duty
note: Labor and welfare wings exist in missions in the Gulf and elsewhere by administrative decision; the Act creates no such duty.

value_label: Complaints lead to administrative sanctions or refunds of fees, but compensation needs the ordinary courts
note: Protectors of Emigrants can suspend or cancel an agent's certificate and forfeit the guarantee; compensation needs the courts.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions whose terms apply to women only (higher minimum ages, consent requirements, bans)
note: Since 2007 women under 30 holding ECR passports are not granted clearance to work in the ECR countries; the rule applies to women only.
source: MEA FAQ and guidelines on emigration clearance; parliamentary answers

value_label: Reintegration rests on policy or programs without a statutory duty
note: No statutory reintegration duty at the national level; states such as Kerala run reintegration schemes (NORKA).

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Licensing by the Bureau with a bank guarantee; licences can be cancelled; no joint liability with the employer.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: Agency fees are regulated by the Bureau; employers bear recruitment costs for domestic workers under the standard contract; other workers pay capped fees.

value_label: A written contract with minimum terms set or verified by the state is required for every worker before departure
note: Registration requires an approved contract; standard contracts are set for domestic workers in the main destinations.

value_label: Orientation is compulsory but may be charged to the worker, or compulsory only for some categories
note: Training with a certificate is compulsory for domestic workers; orientation for other categories; fees may apply.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: Registration includes compulsory insurance and contributions to the Workers' Welfare Fund, which pays for death, disability and repatriation and supports families.

value_label: Officers are posted by administrative decision or policy, without a statutory duty
note: Labor welfare sections are placed in missions by the Bureau and the ministry; a statutory duty was not found.

value_label: Complaints lead to administrative sanctions or refunds of fees, but compensation needs the ordinary courts
note: The Bureau conciliates, inquires into complaints and can order refunds and cancel licences; compensation beyond fees needs the courts.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions whose terms apply to women only (higher minimum ages, consent requirements, bans)
note: Minimum ages for women in domestic work (21 under the 2022 revision, higher for some destinations in earlier rules); the Family Background Report for mothers of young children was removed in 2022.
source: Newsfirst 21 Jun 2022; Daily FT, Cabinet decision 2022

value_label: Reintegration rests on policy or programs without a statutory duty
note: The Sub-Policy and National Action Plan on Return and Reintegration (2015) rests on policy, not statute.

value_label: Recruiters must be licensed and can be sanctioned, but are not jointly liable for the employer's obligations
note: Overseas Employment Promoters need a licence and a security deposit, which can be forfeited; the public Overseas Employment Corporation also recruits; no joint liability with the employer.

value_label: Fees are capped by law, or prohibited only for listed occupations or destinations
note: Service charges are capped by the Rules; charging more is an offense.

value_label: A contract is required, but only for some categories of workers, or without minimum terms or verification
note: Registration with a Protector of Emigrants requires a work visa and an employment contract, but the law sets no minimum terms.

value_label: Orientation is compulsory but may be charged to the worker, or compulsory only for some categories
note: Briefing at the Protectorate at registration is required; formal training is not compulsory.

value_label: A statutory fund or compulsory insurance covers all registered workers for death, disability and repatriation, and funds legal or welfare assistance abroad
note: Registration requires contributions to the Overseas Pakistanis Foundation and a compulsory insurance policy covering death and disability; the Foundation repatriates bodies and supports families.

value_label: Officers are posted by administrative decision or policy, without a statutory duty
note: Community Welfare Attachés are posted by the Ministry; the Ordinance creates no such duty.

value_label: Complaints lead to administrative sanctions or refunds of fees, but compensation needs the ordinary courts
note: Protectors of Emigrants and the Bureau act on complaints against promoters and forfeit deposits; offenses go to the Federal Investigation Agency and the courts.

feature_name: Exit without sex- or age-specific restrictions
value_label: Restrictions whose terms apply to women only (higher minimum ages, consent requirements, bans)
note: The Rules set a minimum age for women going abroad as domestic workers: 35 until July 2025, now 25; the rule applies to women only.
source: Emigration Rules 1979 r. 25 as amended 2025; ProPakistani, 30 Jul 2025

value_label: Reintegration rests on policy or programs without a statutory duty
note: The 2020 National Emigration and Welfare Policy commits to reintegration; no statutory duty was found.
